title: Modernize inflight window tracker and lease eviction policy for latency stability
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current inflight-window tracker and lease eviction policy were implemented as incremental patches over multiple quarters. This has led to unpredictable tail latency when request size distributions spike and to periodic KV-lease churn during minor GC events. Goal: Replace the ad-hoc trackers with a single metered inflight window component, introduce a temperature-based eviction score that factors request TTL, KV-hit recency, and workload affinity, and simplify the lease state machine to remove race-prone transitions. This should reduce p99 latency and KV eviction-induced cold misses while keeping CPU overhead minimal.
acceptance_criteria: Unified inflight-window component replaces legacy inflight counters and is feature-flag guarded
Temperature-based eviction reduces KV cache miss rate by >= 10% on synthetic hotkey workloads
P99 latency for mixed short/long sequences improves by >= 5% in our canary region under 95th percentile load
No increase in steady-state CPU utilization beyond 3% on observed production traces
All new code covered by unit and integration tests; e2e smoke test in CI passes
Graceful rollback path behind runtime feature flag
design_notes: See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Inflight+Window+and+Eviction+Modernization. Key ideas: a circular window index (compact memory), per-shard temperature sketch (approximate recency + size-weighted score), lease lifecycle simplified to (PENDING -> ACTIVE -> GRACE -> RELEASED), and explicit lease acquisition priorities for latency-critical routes. Chosen data structures favor single-writer shards to minimize atomic operations. We evaluated a few heuristics: LRU, LFU with decay, recency-weighted TTL. We picked recency-weighted TTL with size penalties because it best matched observed model session patterns.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — implemented prototype inflight window counter and microbench harness. Observed 2.8% p99 latency drop in synthetic short-req benchmark.

2026-03-01: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Action items: add shard-level telemetry, expose eviction-score histogram, and add a lease preemption backoff to avoid oscillation (assigned to Mateo).
2026-03-06: Implemented temperature sketch and integrated with existing KV API. Added feature flag runtime.enable_new_inflight. Unit tests added for score computation edge cases.

2026-03-10: Canary canary-1 deployment started behind feature flag for 24h. Early telemetry: KV miss rate on hotkey trace reduced ~12%, but a rare case shows increased lease churn during autoscaler spike. Root cause: preemption/backoff not tuned for bursty prewarm. Added mitigation task to tune backoff windows.
2026-03-13: PR opened for scheduler changes and lease state simplification. PR link included below. Planning 48h extended canary while we collect flamegraphs and heap profiles.

benchmarks: Microbench (local harness): mixed-reqs p99 -3.2% with prototype temperature-sketch vs baseline
Canary-1 (24h): hotkey workload KV miss rate -12%, steady-state CPU +1.4%
Stress test (autoscaler spike): observed lease churn increase; mitigated by backoff tuning gives churn back to baseline
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: New eviction logic could evict items needed by long-running inference sessions. Mitigation: route-aware pinning and grace window plus canary monitoring
Risk: Feature flag rollback complexity. Mitigation: implement dual-read path in cache API to allow immediate switch while still serving pinned entries
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: aggregate histograms at shard-level and sample detailed traces only during canary
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit/integration tests and internal perf harness (complete)
Phase 1: Canary-1 (single region, feature flag) for 72h with deep sampling (in progress)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp across two additional regions with 10% traffic steps over 7 days
Phase 3: Full rollout if canary KPIs hold; otherwise rollback and revert PRs
